items.stem: Describe the events of the menstrual cycle with the changes in the ovary, uterus and hormone levels. What happens if fertilisation does not occur?
items.answer: Menstrual phase (days 1–5): breakdown of endometrium. Follicular phase: primary follicles grow into a Graafian follicle; endometrium regenerates; LH and FSH rise gradually, oestrogen secreted. Ovulation (~day 14): LH surge ruptures the Graafian follicle. Luteal phase: corpus luteum secretes progesterone that maintains the endometrium. Without fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone falls and menstruation starts again.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each phase; 1 mark no-fertilisation outcome.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about gametogenesis is correct?
items.answer: The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis.
items.markingKey: (a) The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis. The other statements are false. Meiosis is unequal; one ovum and polar bodies form. Spermatids are haploid; they form after meiosis II. LH acts on Leydig cells to stimulate androgen secretion; FSH acts on Sertoli cells.
options: The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis.
FSH acts on the Leydig cells.
Each primary oocyte gives four functional ova.
Spermatids are diploid.

items.stem: How many sperms are formed from 200 primary spermatocytes? Explain.
items.answer: 800 sperms
items.markingKey: Each primary spermatocyte completes meiosis I and II to give 4 spermatids, each forming a sperm (1) ⇒ 200 × 4 = 800 sperms (1).

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of development in the human foetus: ready for delivery (9 months), eyelids separate (24 weeks), limbs and digits (2 months), first movements and hair on head (5 months). Give a reason.
items.answer: limbs and digits (2 months) → first movements and hair on head (5 months) → eyelids separate (24 weeks) → ready for delivery (9 months)
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order limbs and digits (2 months) → first movements and hair on head (5 months) → eyelids separate (24 weeks) → ready for delivery (9 months); 1 mark for the reason: Milestones as described in NCERT.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The corpus luteum secretes FSH.”
items.answer: It secretes large amounts of progesterone.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It secretes large amounts of progesterone.

items.stem: Which of the following is a layer of the uterine wall?
items.answer: myometrium
items.markingKey: (b) Myometrium is a layer of the uterine wall; the others are not.
options: bulbourethral glands
myometrium
ampulla
prostate

items.stem: Define the term “the zona pellucida”.
items.answer: The new membrane formed around the secondary oocyte in the Graafian follicle.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the new membrane formed around the secondary oocyte in the Graafian follicle.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Spermatogenesis starts before birth.
Reason (R): Spermatogenesis starts at puberty under GnRH.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false; spermatogenesis begins at puberty.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: In a regular 28-day menstrual cycle, which phase is Aditi's body in on day 9?
items.answer: follicular (proliferative) phase
items.markingKey: (b) Day 9: follicular (proliferative) phase – primary follicles grow into a Graafian follicle and the endometrium regenerates under rising LH, FSH and oestrogen.
options: luteal (secretory) phase
follicular (proliferative) phase
ovulatory phase
menstrual phase

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Testes are situated outside the abdominal cavity.
Reason (R): Spermatogenesis needs a temperature about 2–2.5 °C lower than body temperature.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) The scrotum maintains this.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of phases of the menstrual cycle: ovulation, menstrual phase, luteal phase. Give a reason.
items.answer: menstrual phase → ovulation → luteal phase
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order menstrual phase → ovulation → luteal phase; 1 mark for the reason: Menstruation lasts 3–5 days, ovulation is near day 14 and the luteal phase follows.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about pregnancy, embryonic development, parturition and lactation is correct?
items.answer: The heart of the embryo forms after one month of pregnancy.
items.markingKey: (c) The heart of the embryo forms after one month of pregnancy. The other statements are false. It secretes hCG, hPL, oestrogens and progestogens. It is induced by a neuroendocrine mechanism involving oxytocin. Eyelids separate and eyelashes form by the end of about 24 weeks (second trimester).
options: By the end of the first trimester the foetus opens its eyelids.
Parturition is induced by prolactin.
The heart of the embryo forms after one month of pregnancy.
The placenta does not secrete any hormones.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about gametogenesis is incorrect?
items.answer: Each primary oocyte gives four functional ova.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “Each primary oocyte gives four functional ova.” Correct form: Meiosis is unequal; one ovum and polar bodies form.
options: Spermatogenesis starts at puberty due to increased GnRH.
Each primary oocyte gives four functional ova.
The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis.
The middle piece of the sperm has numerous mitochondria.

items.stem: Explain the term “the mammary lobes”.
items.answer: The 15–20 masses of glandular tissue in each breast containing alveoli that secrete milk.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the 15–20 masses of glandular tissue in each breast containing alveoli that secrete milk.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Each testis has about 250 compartments called testicular lobules.
Reason (R): The endometrium is the outer layer of the uterus.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: The perimetrium is outer; the endometrium is the inner glandular layer.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A hormone involved in pregnancy or birth has this role: detected in pregnancy tests; secreted by the placenta. Identify the hormone. Give a reason.
items.answer: HCG
items.markingKey: 1 mark: hCG; 1 mark: the features detected in pregnancy tests; secreted by the placenta are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct path of sperms from the testis: epididymis, ejaculatory duct, seminiferous tubules. Give a reason.
items.answer: seminiferous tubules → epididymis → ejaculatory duct
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order seminiferous tubules → epididymis → ejaculatory duct; 1 mark for the reason: Sperms are stored in the epididymis and leave via vas deferens and urethra.

items.stem: Which term describes the structural and functional unit between the developing embryo and the maternal body?
items.answer: the placenta
items.markingKey: (a) The placenta: the structural and functional unit between the developing embryo and the maternal body.
options: the placenta
the umbilical cord
the foetal ejection reflex
the chorionic villi

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The inner cell mass forms the placenta.
Reason (R): The trophoblast layer attaches to the endometrium during implantation.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: The trophoblast attaches to the endometrium; the inner cell mass differentiates into the embryo. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “Each primary oocyte gives four functional ova.”
items.answer: Meiosis is unequal; one ovum and polar bodies form.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Meiosis is unequal; one ovum and polar bodies form.

items.stem:
A structure of the human reproductive system has these features: fimbriae collect the ovum; about 10–12 cm long; site of fertilisation.
(i) Identify the structure. (1 mark)
(ii) State one more feature you would expect to observe. (1 mark)
(iii) How would the observations differ if it were the seminal vesicles? Give two points. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) The oviduct (ii) has infundibulum, ampulla and isthmus (iii) paired male accessory glands; open into the ejaculatory duct with vas deferens
items.markingKey: (i) the oviduct – 1 mark. (ii) any one of: has infundibulum, ampulla and isthmus – 1 mark. (iii) for the seminal vesicles: paired male accessory glands; secretion rich in fructose; contribute to seminal plasma – 1 mark each for any two.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about gametogenesis is correct?
items.answer: The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis.
items.markingKey: (d) The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis. The other statements are false. It begins during foetal development; oogonia form and enter prophase I before birth. Spermatids are haploid; they form after meiosis II. The secondary oocyte completes meiosis II only after a sperm enters it.
options: Spermatids are diploid.
Meiosis II in human oocytes is completed before ovulation.
Oogenesis starts at puberty.
The first polar body is formed at the end of meiosis I in oogenesis.

items.stem: How many ova are formed from 500 primary oocytes? Explain.
items.answer: 500 ova
items.markingKey: Meiosis is unequal; each primary oocyte gives one ovum and polar bodies (1) ⇒ 500 × 1 = 500 ova (1).
